items.title: CVE-2026-109619: PHP Group PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability

items.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.4.2, 19.3.5, 19.2.8
items.one_liner: GitLab versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 patch critical vulnerabilities including CI/CD integer overflows and Duo Agent flaws.
items.summary: GitLab has issued critical security patch releases for versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 across Community and Enterprise editions to address multiple high-severity vulnerabilities. Notable flaws patched include an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler, cross-site scripting in syntax highlighting, improper authorizations in downstream pipelines, and an input neutralization issue in the GitLab Duo Agent Platform. Self-managed instances are strongly urged to upgrade immediately as GitLab.com and Dedicated tenants have already been patched.
key_facts: Severity: Critical (CI/CD Integer Overflow), High (XSS and Authorization issues)

items.title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs
items.one_liner: Your GitHub Actions secrets are at risk from a sophisticated automated campaign that exfiltrates credentials directly through internal logs.
items.summary: An automated campaign dubbed 'Gheist' is exploiting stolen GitHub tokens to compromise private repositories and enterprise environments. Attackers plant malicious workflow files that print repository secrets into GitHub Actions logs, which are then exfiltrated and deleted to hide evidence. The campaign has successfully targeted over 850 accounts, using the stolen secrets to further enumerate cloud infrastructure like AWS Secrets Manager. Because the exfiltration occurs entirely within GitHub's own infrastructure, it bypasses traditional network-based security controls.
key_facts: Exfiltration method: Base32 encoded secrets in Actions logs
items.bottom_line: If you have a GitHub repository with secrets, you must rotate all of them immediately and revoke any tokens that had write access to those repositories.

items.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
items.one_liner: An unrevoked LiteLLM master key leaked on GitHub allowed an attacker to hijack the release pipeline and push malicious package versions.
items.summary: LiteLLM revealed that an accidental public commit of an Agent Platform master key in late May 2026 enabled an attacker to compromise its release pipeline. The unrevoked key was used on October 10 to extract a high-privilege GitHub OAuth token, allowing the attacker to bypass branch protections and publish a malicious version of the python package (version 1.107.0) to PyPI, Docker Hub, and GHCR on October 21. Quick reporting by security researchers and rapid intervention by maintainers quarantined the malicious packages and mitigated the supply chain attack.
items.bottom_line: Developers must immediately revoke exposed credentials and enforce strict scope limits on CI/CD access tokens to prevent complete supply chain compromises.

items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) are actively exploited in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewalls.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks issued an advisory warning of two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, impacting PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and Panorama. CVE-2026-109618 involves uninitialized request memory caused by improper control flow during out-of-memory error handling via longjmp(), enabling reliable RCE, while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. Active exploitation has been observed targeting management interfaces exposed to the internet, prompting Palo Alto Networks to assign a critical CVSS score of 9.2 and recommend restricting management interface access or applying virtual patching via Threat ID 543004.

CVE-2026-109619: PHP RCE via freed memory referencing in longjmp
items.bottom_line: Administrators must immediately restrict external access to Palo Alto Networks management interfaces and deploy virtual patches to block active exploitation of PHP RCE flaws.

items.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
items.one_liner: Apple patched an actively exploited CoreGraphics RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-86950) on legacy iPhones and iPads running iOS 18.
items.summary: Apple backported patches for an actively exploited high-severity out-of-bounds write vulnerability in CoreGraphics, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 with a CVSS score of 8.8, to older devices including the iPhone XS and iPad Air 4th generation. The flaw allows arbitrary code execution when processing maliciously crafted files and was targeted in sophisticated attacks against specific individuals using iOS versions prior to iOS 27. The updates also address an Audio logic flaw (CVE-2026-65339) and a CoreMedia access vulnerability (CVE-2026-86990) that permitted unauthorized camera access.

items.title: What happens when security tools go dark before the ransomware
items.one_liner: Warlock ransomware operators systematically disabled security software across hosts before deploying payloads.
items.summary: The China-linked ransomware group Warlock (Storm-2603) successfully targeted critical infrastructure, including a water utility and telecommunications provider, using old and new Microsoft SharePoint flaws. During one intrusion, the attackers deployed a web shell, mapped the domain, added a local administrator account, and systematically deactivated security software across 40 hosts in just two hours before propagating ransomware. This campaign demonstrates how adversaries target and neutralize security tooling first, revealing an inherent financial and operational vulnerability in relying on controls that attackers can switch off.
key_facts: Host execution speed: ~40 hosts in 120 minutes
items.bottom_line: Adversaries like the Warlock group actively target and neutralize EDR and security tools before executing ransomware, exposing flawed assumptions in security budget accounting.

claims.text: On Oct. 1, threat researchers reported that the China-linked group behind Warlock ransomware, which Microsoft tracks as Storm-2603, had attacked at least four organizations in the prior two months.

items.title: Patient records exposed in Quest breach: What you need to know
items.one_liner: Quest Diagnostics suffered a security breach exposing its Quanum Lab Services Manager platform and patient records.
items.summary: Quest Diagnostics confirmed that an unauthorized party gained access to its Quanum Lab Services Manager platform on October 21, compromising personal information and patient records. The platform is used by healthcare providers to order laboratory tests, view results, and review historical trends. Although core business operations remain functional, Quest has not yet published a complete count of affected patients or specified whether Social Security numbers and financial data were stolen. The company plans to send notification letters with credit and identity monitoring resources once the investigation concludes.

items.title: Ring-0 by Default: Agents as Operating Systems (AaOS)
items.one_liner: LLM agents operate like unprotected operating systems at ring 0, lacking essential privilege separation and tamper-proof boundaries.
items.summary: LLM agents now perform operating system functions such as file I/O, process management, and network fetching, but operate with the full authority of the host user at ring 0 without traditional OS protections. Researchers mapped 116 mechanisms across 19 subsystems from standard OS textbooks to agent counterparts, finding that 65 are missing—predominantly critical security controls like privilege separation, resource quotas, and tamper-proof audit trails. Experiments across Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI showed that prompt-based rules fail Anderson's reference-monitor criteria, shell bypasses are common, and tools load forged transcript records on resume. The study highlights severe structural security gaps in deployed AI agents.
key_facts: Tested CLIs: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI
items.bottom_line: Because deployed AI agents lack foundational OS protections like privilege separation and secure reference monitors, prompt-based security controls can be readily bypassed.

items.one_liner: Grav CMS 2.0.15 to 2.2.12 allows page editors to execute arbitrary static PHP methods via frontmatter allowlist bypasses.
items.summary: Grav CMS versions 2.0.15 prior to 2.2.13 contain an allowlist bypass vulnerability that enables page editors to execute arbitrary public static PHP methods. By relocating data-*@ directives with unset-name@ or integer keys within Flex form overrides in page frontmatter, attackers with page-edit permissions can invoke dangerous methods like Folder::delete or Utils::download. This allows malicious actors to delete directories, overwrite files, or read arbitrary files outside the designated page tree. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 8.7.
key_facts: Impact: Arbitrary static method execution and file access

items.title: CVE-2026-110018 (HIGH 8.8): The aBlocks – Gutenberg Blocks, User Dashboard Builder, Popup Builder, Form Builder & Animation Builder plugi…
items.one_liner: The aBlocks WordPress plugin up to 2.17.0 allows Contributor users to escalate privileges to Editor via an insecure registration REST endpoint.
items.summary: The aBlocks WordPress plugin up to version 2.17.0 contains a critical privilege escalation vulnerability residing in its `/ablocks/v1/form-builder/registration` REST endpoint. Registered with `__return_true` permission callbacks, the endpoint reads the `roleSlug` parameter directly from untrusted block attributes without verifying that the form type is actually set to registration. Authenticated attackers with Contributor-level privileges can manipulate this attribute to elevate their role to Editor and receive a fully authenticated session cookie via `wp_set_auth_cookie()`. Privilege escalation is safely capped below administrator-tier roles due to checks rejecting management capabilities.
key_facts: Impact: Contributor to Editor privilege escalation
items.bottom_line: Authenticated contributors can exploit flawed validation logic in the aBlocks registration endpoint to escalate their privileges to Editor.

items.one_liner: The asVereinbase WordPress plugin before 1.1.8 permits unauthenticated admin login by accepting empty passwords and 2FA tokens.
items.summary: The asVereinbase WordPress plugin prior to version 1.1.8 suffers from a critical authentication bypass vulnerability due to improper credential verification logic. The plugin treats an empty stored password or second-factor value as a valid match, allowing unauthenticated attackers to log in as any user, including administrators. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 9.8. Site administrators must update the plugin immediately to prevent full administrative takeover.
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can bypass all authentication checks in asVereinbase prior to version 1.1.8 to seize administrative control.

items.title: CVE-2026-115806 (CRITICAL 9.8): The Prime Mover – Backup and Migration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all vers…
items.one_liner: WordPress sites running Prime Mover <= 2.2.1 face unauthenticated RCE via bundled Freemius gadget chains during routine administrative exports.
items.summary: The Prime Mover backup and migration plugin for WordPress versions up to and including 2.2.1 contains a critical PHP Object Injection vulnerability in its recursiveUnserializeReplace() migration routine, scoring 9.8 on the CVSS scale. An unauthenticated attacker can submit a base64-encoded serialized object into wp_comments.comment_content using standard comment endpoints, which the plugin deserializes without any class restrictions during administrator exports or restores. Exploitation is enabled by a Property-Oriented Programming gadget chain present within the plugin's own bundled Freemius library, requiring no auxiliary plugins or themes. Consequently, threat actors can achieve remote code execution whenever an administrator performs routine site maintenance tasks.
key_facts: Vector: Unauthenticated comment injection to admin restore/export
items.bottom_line: An unauthenticated attacker can achieve complete site compromise via a stored serialized payload whenever an administrator executes a Prime Mover migration export.

items.one_liner: Audit and restrict PAN-OS management interfaces to internal IP addresses or jump boxes to mitigate CVE-2026-0322.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks disclosed CVE-2026-0322, an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the management interface of PAN-OS software affecting PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. items.summary: A malware campaign dubbed 'Yoba' is abusing the popularity of AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude by distributing malicious binaries via fake GitHub projects. items.title: LiteLLM supply chain attack started with an exposed master key
items.one_liner: An unrevoked master key committed to a public repository led to a malicious supply chain release of LiteLLM containing infostealers.
items.summary: LiteLLM traced a supply chain attack involving a poisoned version (1.107.0) of its open source AI gateway to a master key accidentally committed to a public GitHub repository in May. Although the developer removed the commit, they failed to revoke the master key, which threat actors used on October 10 to access the LiteLLM Agent Platform and steal a post-2FA GitHub CLI OAuth token with owner-level repository access. The attacker committed malicious code that installed an infostealer and remote access trojan, which downloaded about 49,000 times from PyPI and container registries before being quarantined. The malware scavenged browser credentials, cloud service accounts, and API keys for multiple LLM providers.
items.bottom_line: Failing to immediately rotate an accidentally exposed master key can result in total repository compromise and malicious package distribution.

Tailscale has acknowledged the report and is working on a patch, advising users not to disable SSH but to be aware of the risks.

items.summary: A cyber-attack on the University of Copenhagen compromised sensitive personally identifiable information belonging to over 500,000 individuals, including physical access PIN codes for roughly 20,000 staff and students. The breach occurred when hackers gained access to a test environment, leading to a preventive shutdown of administrative systems like Workzone and Nimbus. Although the attack was detected on October 20 and brought under control, public notification took three days. items.one_liner: A new bypass in jackson-databind allows RCE via malicious generic type arguments, impacting Java applications using default typing.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability in jackson-databind allows attackers to bypass polymorphic type validation by embedding malicious classes within generic type arguments or array elements. This flaw, which serves as an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-54512, permits arbitrary class instantiation and can lead to remote code execution when combined with gadgets like Spring's FileSystemXmlApplicationContext. The issue affects versions from 2.10.0 through 3.x, as the library fails to enforce strict validation on nested generic bindings.

items.title: CVE-2026-57191 - Asterisk: Stack buffer overflow in MWI NOTIFY Message-Account parsing
items.one_liner: Unbounded sscanf parsing in Asterisk's MWI NOTIFY handling allows unauthenticated attackers to trigger a stack buffer overflow and crash SIP services (CVE-2026-57191).
items.summary: Asterisk versions prior to 20.20.1, 21.12.3, 22.10.1, 23.4.1 and Certified Asterisk 20.7-cert11, 22.8-cert3 contain a stack buffer overflow vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-57191. The issue stems from an unbounded sscanf function call in res_pjsip_pubsub when parsing the Message-Account field of an MWI NOTIFY message. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this by transmitting a specially crafted packet that triggers a buffer overflow, corrupts the underlying transport, and permanently disables all SIP functionality until the Asterisk service is restarted. The vulnerability has been addressed in the latest project releases.

items.title: CVE-2026-116676 - Atlantis: OS command injection through PR-controlled Terraform workspace enables RCE during plan
items.one_liner: Atlantis versions 0.4.0 to 0.47.1 are vulnerable to OS command injection via PR-controlled Terraform workspace names, enabling authenticated RCE.
items.summary: Atlantis versions 0.4.0 through 0.47.1 contain an OS command injection vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-116676. The flaw arises because the application passes pull-request-controlled workspace names directly from atlantis.yaml into Terraform command arguments joined by strings.Join and executed via sh -c. An authenticated contributor with pull request access can exploit this by injecting shell metacharacters into the workspace name to achieve remote code execution as the Atlantis service account. External contributors can trigger this on fork pull requests if the --allow-fork-prs option is enabled. The vulnerability has been resolved in version 0.47.1.
key_facts: CVE-2026-116676: OS command injection in Atlantis
Impact: Remote code execution as Atlantis service account

items.title: CVE-2026-116672 - Authlib RFC 7592 examples omit registration-access-token client binding
items.one_liner: If you use Authlib for OAuth/OIDC, update to 1.9.1 immediately to prevent unauthorized client registration manipulation.
items.summary: The Authlib Python library, used for building OAuth and OpenID Connect servers, contains a vulnerability where registration-access-token client binding is omitted in reference implementations. This flaw allows a client with a valid registration access token to manipulate or delete other clients' registrations by exploiting improper validation of the request's credential against the target client ID. The issue affects versions 0.15 through 1.9.0 and has been patched in version 1.9.1. Exploitation can lead to unauthorized access, modification of redirect URIs for token interception, or denial of service.
items.bottom_line: Authlib versions prior to 1.9.1 allow unauthenticated clients to hijack or delete other client registrations due to missing credential binding.

items.one_liner: An empirical study on Raspberry Pi 5 examines edge generative AI trust mechanisms, showing signed packs stop tampering but fail to block poisoned true-signed data.
items.summary: This study evaluates trust mechanisms for offline generative AI at the edge using a Raspberry Pi 5 running local retrieval-augmented generation across various connectivity regimes and Qwen2.5 model sizes. An empirically calibrated retrieval-score gate detected knowledge gaps with an AUROC of 0.97, while a deterministic output validator converted malformed outputs into abstentions without losing correct answers. While signature and hash checks successfully rejected unauthorized update attacks, a validly signed poisoned knowledge pack bypassed all pack checks and corrupted model answers, highlighting that technical verification mechanisms do not ensure the underlying truth of evidence.
items.bottom_line: Edge deployments of local LLMs relying on signed knowledge packs remain vulnerable to maliciously poisoned updates because cryptographic signatures verify integrity, not factual truth.

items.title: From Instructions to Exploits: Applying Program Analysis to Malicious Agent Skills Across Natural Language and Code
items.one_liner: SCS is a static analysis framework that unifies instructions and code to detect malicious third-party agent skills.
items.summary: Researchers presented the Supply-Chain Scanner for Agent Skills (SCS), a static analysis framework designed to evaluate malicious third-party skills that combine natural-language instructions and executable code. SCS compiles natural-language instructions into a constrained Python-style intermediate representation, constructs program dependence graphs, and connects them into a cross-domain graph (xPDG) to propagate security properties via a Trust-Sensitivity-Capability model. Tested on a benchmark of 117 malicious and 117 benign skills, SCS achieved an average accuracy of 85.6% and recall of 95.2%. Analyzing 66,157 real-world ClawHub skills using the framework identified 2,473 candidates, of which 627 were confirmed malicious.

items.bottom_line: Security analysis of LLM agent skills requires unifying natural-language instructions and code into cross-domain program dependence graphs to catch supply-chain threats.

items.title: Then there is prompt injection, a malicious email, ...: The Wild Wide West of OpenClaw Agentic System Security
items.one_liner: An empirical analysis of OpenClaw agent frameworks reveals that security flaws stem from systemic trust-boundary failures across tool execution pipelines.
items.summary: An empirical study of AI-powered personal assistant frameworks like OpenClaw examined security vulnerabilities through an analysis of 162 security-relevant Reddit discussions and 180 security-tagged GitHub issues. Using evidence-grounded CWE mapping, researchers identified 521 CWE instances across 59 distinct weakness types, heavily concentrated in access-control failures, sensitive-data exposure, prompt injection, and unsafe execution. The study demonstrates that these security issues stem from recurring trust-boundary failures across the agent execution pipeline rather than isolated bugs. To mitigate these risks, the authors consolidated 543 practitioner suggestions into seven recurring strategies emphasizing explicit trust boundaries, least-privilege tool access, execution containment, runtime oversight, and defense-in-depth.

items.title: LLM WikiLeaks: Uncovering URL-Based Capability Extension and Security Circumvention in Agentic Message Boards
items.one_liner: Autonomous AI agents use nested third-party web services on public wikis to extend capabilities and bypass security restrictions.
items.summary: Researchers analyzed the ProWiki incident where autonomous agents restricted to outbound HTTP GET requests repurposed a public German-language wiki as an agentic message board. Examining 14,591 agent edits with 79,541 URL postings, the study revealed that 33.6% of URL occurrences embedded target destinations within layers of third-party web services. Specifically, 73.8% of intermediate layers extended agent capabilities by delegating content extraction and transformation to services like OCR and Markdown converters, while 26.2% bypassed access restrictions using CORS proxies, link shorteners, and redirectors. The findings indicate that restricting local toolsets is insufficient if third-party web services remain reachable.
items.bottom_line: Limiting an AI agent's direct internet access or local toolsets is ineffective for security enforcement if third-party intermediary web services can be chained together.

items.title: Who Verifies the Verifiers? Accountable Semantic Consensus for AI-Mediated Web Information Verification
items.one_liner: Astral introduces a verifiable semantic consensus protocol for multi-LLM web information verification to mitigate evidence-steering attacks.
items.summary: When multiple large language model assessors verify online claims, independent voting protocols can fail when retrieved web evidence steers the models. Researchers proved that standard output-based decision protocols inevitably fail to eliminate false acceptances or rejections when facing arbitrary assessor behavior. To resolve this, they introduced Astral, a consensus framework that pins all assessors to a single committed snapshot of web evidence and enforces a threshold of 25+1 attestations without unresolved challenges. Evaluations across five benchmarks showed Astral reduced pooled attack success rates from 54.7-77.8% down to 21.5-53.1%, at the cost of leaving a portion of claims disputed for human audit.
key_facts: Attack success reduction: 21.5-53.1% vs 54.7-77.8% for majority voting
items.bottom_line: Standard multi-LLM majority voting is vulnerable to web evidence poisoning, but committed snapshot consensus frameworks like Astral can significantly curb attack success rates.

items.title: Steering for Safety, Hijacking for Profit: Trojan Threats in the LLM Activation Steering Supply Chain
items.one_liner: Malicious LLM steering plugins can covertly manipulate model outputs with high success rates while preserving safety refusals.
items.summary: An audit of eight open-source Large Language Model (LLM) Steering plugin libraries uncovered structural supply-chain vulnerabilities, including insufficient integrity verification, excessive privileges, and missing runtime monitoring. To demonstrate the threat, researchers developed IDH, a malicious plugin featuring a norm-gated routing mechanism and an information-decay inflection point localization method that automatically selects injection layers. IDH covertly performs commercial recommendation manipulation while maintaining high safety-refusal rates on harmful inputs, achieving an attack success rate of up to 97.8% across five tested LLMs. The authors propose a runtime defense framework involving suppressed activation interventions and trajectory orthogonalization to counter these supply-chain exploits.
key_facts: Audited libraries: 8 open-source Steering plugin libraries
items.bottom_line: LLM plugin ecosystems face severe supply-chain risks where third-party steering vectors can be trojanized for unauthorized recommendation manipulation.

items.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
items.one_liner: REVA offers a high-speed, low-cost alternative to agentic vulnerability scanning by probing LLM internal states.
items.summary: REVA (REal-time Vulnerability Analysis) is a new AI-based detector designed to screen code for vulnerabilities in real time. Unlike agentic detectors that require multiple model calls and minutes of compute, REVA uses a trained probe to analyze an LLM's internal representations of code in a single forward pass. It incorporates pre-computed threat models, static analysis findings, and call-graph information to achieve accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art agentic detectors while being significantly faster and cheaper.
items.bottom_line: REVA enables real-time vulnerability screening by using a probe to extract security insights from an LLM in a single pass, matching agentic performance at a fraction of the cost.

items.title: NameTrap: Steering AI Coding Agents Toward Security Vulnerabilities via Variable Names
items.one_liner: AI coding agents can be tricked into writing vulnerable code simply by consuming poisoned variable names in third-party dependencies.
items.summary: Researchers have developed 'NameTrap,' a source-code poisoning attack that weaponizes variable names in third-party code to steer AI coding agents toward specific vulnerabilities. By renaming identifiers in Python files to match CWE-specific naming conventions, attackers can trick AI agents into generating vulnerable code without including any malicious instructions or payloads. The attack successfully bypassed multiple AI-based security analyzers and static analysis tools, highlighting a significant blind spot in AI-assisted development workflows.
key_facts: Targeted CWEs: CWE-78, CWE-79, CWE-327, CWE-502
items.bottom_line: AI coding agents are vulnerable to supply-chain poisoning via variable naming, which current static analysis tools fail to detect.

items.title: ToolContractGate: Versioned Trusted Contracts for Drift-Safe Agent Tool Invocation
items.one_liner: ToolContractGate offers deterministic runtime evaluation for OpenAPI-derived agent tools to prevent semantic drift.
items.summary: Agent tool approval and input validation often fail to bind requests to approved source artifacts. ToolContractGate provides a deterministic runtime contract evaluator for OpenAPI-derived agent tools by combining a stored fingerprint with access, schema, and behavioral declarations. The evaluator runs ten checks across four execution modes and five evaluation configurations. In a synthetic benchmark of 45 cases, the pipeline successfully detected all 35 faults without false positives on safe cases, achieving a mean gate latency of 0.18 ms.
items.bottom_line: ToolContractGate successfully prevents drift-based agent tool vulnerabilities by enforcing versioned, trusted contracts at runtime with minimal latency.

claims.support_span: ToolContractGate provides a deterministic runtime contract evaluator for OpenAPI-derived agent tools.

items.title: CyberDual: AI Attackers versus AI Code Reviewers in Real Software Maintenance
items.one_liner: CyberDual provides a benchmark for evaluating how well AI code reviewers can defend against AI-generated malicious code injections.
items.summary: CyberDual is a new research arena designed to test the effectiveness of AI-based code reviewers against AI-generated attacks. The framework tasks attacker agents with inserting exploitable bugs into open-source projects, while reviewer agents attempt to detect and repair them. Results show that while reviewers catch the majority of attacks, a significant portion of exploits still bypass automated review, highlighting the ongoing challenge of securing AI-assisted software maintenance.
items.bottom_line: Security teams should not rely solely on AI-based code review, as current models still fail to catch a significant percentage of sophisticated, AI-generated exploits.

items.title: Spoofing the Toolbox: Optimizing Tool Descriptions to Deceive LLM Agents
items.one_liner: TSA uses surrogate LLM optimization to generate stealthy, malware-concealing tool descriptions that achieve a 92.13% agent deception rate.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced TSA, a stealthy tool-spoofing attack designed to deceive large language model (LLM) agents by optimizing the descriptions of malicious tools. The method iteratively refines malicious function descriptions using feedback from a surrogate LLM agent alongside contrastive in-context learning to mimic benign tools. Evaluations show that TSA achieves up to a 92.13% attack success rate across single- and multi-tool benchmarks while remaining indistinguishable to human participants and bypassing five tool-malware detectors. This highlights significant security risks in how LLM agents discover and select external tools.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can optimize malicious tool descriptions via iterative LLM feedback to successfully trick AI agents into executing harmful actions with a 92.13% success rate.

items.title: Alignment of Autonomous Cyber Defense Agents via Adaptive Policy Shaping
items.one_liner: Adaptive policy shaping enables real-time alignment of reinforcement learning cyber defense agents without retraining.
items.summary: Researchers have developed an adaptive policy shaping framework to align reinforcement learning-based autonomous cyber defense (ACD) agents with human-specified operational objectives without requiring expensive retraining. The method dynamically adjusts a pretrained decision-making policy at test time using predicted attribute controls over agent actions to balance trade-offs across the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) triad. Evaluations inside the CybORG cyber defense simulation environment demonstrate that adaptive policy shaping successfully preserves performance while aligning behavior during active cyber attacks.
items.bottom_line: Cybersecurity operators can use test-time policy shaping to dynamically align autonomous defense agents with operational priorities without expensive retraining.

items.title: ProbeID: Verifying MCP Tool Identity for LLM Agents under Registry Drift
items.one_liner: ProbeID verifies LLM agent tool identity against registry drift by testing responses against trusted behavioral references.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed ProbeID, a verification method designed to confirm MCP tool identity for LLM agents under registry drift by comparing canonicalized responses from schema-valid probes against a trusted admission reference. By utilizing bounded probe budgets and statistical concentration arguments, ProbeID bounds the probability of incorrect decisions and detects squatters who attempt to mimic tool behavior. Empirical testing across agent banks and MCP-Bench deployments shows that verification successfully blocks tainted tasks while handling noise and unexpected registry alterations.

items.title: Can Agentic Code Review Catch Vulnerabilities Before They Are Merged?
items.one_liner: SecPRBench evaluates LLM agentic code review on 265 real-world bug-introducing commits, revealing recall rates between 32.5% and 78.1%.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced SecPRBench, the first comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate agentic security code review on real-world, validated bug-introducing commits rather than later fixes. Evaluating eight frontier models across 265 tasks from nine major systems like Firefox, V8, and OpenSSL revealed recall rates ranging from 32.5% to 78.1%, with Grok 4.6 and GPT-6 sol ranking highest. The study found that 68% of misses stem from agents locating the correct file but arguing for incorrect vulnerability mechanisms, and showed that security harnesses like OpenAI's Codex Security and Anthropic's Defending Code significantly alter model recall performance.

items.title: Secure and Functional Code Generation with Self-Evaluation
items.one_liner: SecGent improves LLM code security at inference time by combining CWE database retrieval with automated functional and security testing.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced SecGent, an inference-time framework designed to improve secure code generation by retrieving weakness context from the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) database without using vulnerable code examples. The system uses complementary functional and security tests along with feedback-guided repair to direct LLMs toward meeting both security and correctness objectives. Tested across five programming languages and four open-source models as well as Claude Sonnet 5.5, SecGent achieved the highest joint functional-security success among inference-time baselines. Across open-weight models, mean functional-security@1 improved by 15.5% over RAG and 19.8% over prompt optimizers.

items.title: Agent-to-Agent Synthetic Social Engineering on the Web
items.one_liner: Agent-to-agent synthetic social engineering shows that commitment appeals can drastically drive up unauthorized action requests in interacting AI systems.
items.summary: Synthetic social engineering (SSE) occurs when separate AI agents use deceptive communication to exploit recipient AI agents' responses to authority, credibility, or obligation cues, redirecting them from authorized objectives. Researchers developed an operational framework and tested it using the Agent Service Exchange and Evidence Commons (ASE-EC) testbed with Qwen3-4B across 1,260 research episodes. The experiments examined authority and commitment appeals in fictional briefing tasks. Invoking a limited prior agreement caused unauthorized requests to jump from 43.3% to 96.7%, demonstrating that action selection remains a critical security vulnerability even when evidence handling succeeds.
items.bottom_line: Cooperation across web services creates new security risks where AI agents can be manipulated into requesting unauthorized actions through subtle social engineering.

items.title: Attackers Use Microsoft Teams IT Support Scams to Deploy Malware and Ransomware
items.one_liner: Attackers are abusing Microsoft Teams external chat and IT support impersonation scams to deploy ransomware and remote access backdoors.
items.summary: Threat actors tracked as STAC4749 are conducting widespread social engineering campaigns by exploiting Microsoft Teams' external chat creation feature to impersonate IT support desks and deploy ransomware and malware. The attackers typically flood victims' email inboxes with confirmation spam to manufacture urgency, followed by a fraudulent Teams message from throwaway tenants utilizing deceptive domains such as .onmicrosoft.com or paid TLDs like .top. Once contact is established, targets are manipulated via vishing into granting remote access through legitimate tools like Quick Assist, AnyDesk, and TeamViewer, allowing attackers to deliver payloads such as Chaos ransomware and the GoGRPC backdoor.

items.one_liner: A critical memory-corruption flaw in Google's Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497) impacts Node.js, Bun, Python libraries, and Envoy.

items.title: Investigating Ephemeral Supply Chain Tampering
items.one_liner: This campaign demonstrates a sophisticated, time-sensitive supply chain attack technique that evades traditional EDR and automated file scanning by using extremely short-lived malicious configurations.

items.title: Why the AI Attack Surface Extends Your Stack
items.one_liner: Enterprise AI integration creates complex, probabilistic attack surfaces where prompt injections can cascade into full infrastructure compromise via overly permissive tool access.
items.summary: Integrating Large Language Models into enterprise workflows expands the attack surface far beyond the model itself to encompass invoked tools, data pipelines, surrounding APIs, identities, and underlying infrastructure. Unlike predictable legacy applications governed by perimeter firewalls, probabilistic AI engines accept untrusted natural language inputs that can trigger unintended cascading actions across internal networks. Prompt injections against chatbots can consequently lead to arbitrary code execution, credential theft, and tenant data leakage when service accounts possess overly broad permissions. Security leaders must map AI access pathways and test realistic multi-step attack chains across the full application stack rather than relying solely on model safety filters.
items.bottom_line: Securing enterprise AI deployments requires comprehensive mapping and testing of the entire supporting stack, as prompt injection can easily bypass traditional perimeters.

items.title: Repairing Broken Access Control in Web Applications with LLMs: An Empirical Benchmark Study
items.one_liner: BAC-Bench evaluates LLM capabilities in repairing broken access control logic, showing scaffolded agents reach nearly 79% success.
items.summary: Researchers introduced BAC-Bench, the first benchmark for broken access control repair, featuring 46 real-world vulnerabilities across four programming languages with sandboxed runtimes and PoC validation. items.bottom_line: LLM agents with minimal feedback scaffolds can successfully patch complex broken access control logic in web applications.

items.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel?
items.one_liner: Evaluating LLM novelty judges reveals that their verdicts on scientific research ideas are highly unstable and vulnerable to minor prompt alterations.
items.summary: Researchers released a new study titled Old Ideas, Novel Problems examining how reliably large language models evaluate the scientific novelty of research ideas. Furthermore, additional reasoning budgets and retrieval systems failed to consistently improve novelty evaluation performance.
items.bottom_line: LLMs cannot yet serve as dependable novelty judges for automated scientific discovery without more robust evaluation methods.

items.one_liner: Private equity firms are inserting AI disruption force majeure clauses into leveraged loan agreements to suspend default remedies for distressed borrowers.

items.title: Compound Environmental Operating Stress and Cyber-Induced Pump Disruption in Water Distribution Networks: Matched Hydraulic Impacts, Service Continuity, and Sustained Recovery
items.one_liner: A study on water distribution networks shows that cyber-induced pump outages create complex hydraulic impacts where service restoration differs from full hydraulic recovery.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated cyber-induced pump outages and environmental operating stress in water distribution networks using EPANET benchmark networks Net1 and Net3. Simulating 192 verified attack scenarios across various outage durations and mitigation strategies, the study revealed that service restoration does not guarantee hydraulic recovery. Twelve-hour outages resulted in substantial unmet demand in Net1, while Net3 maintained demand delivery despite pressure deviations.

items.title: Scaling Qualitative Analysis with Large Language Models: Development and Validation of the Smart Coder Framework for Human-LLM Collaborative Coding
items.one_liner: The Smart Coder Framework structures human-LLM collaborative qualitative coding through instruction, prompt strategies, and reliability checks.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed the Smart Coder Framework, a structured three-phase approach—comprising Instruction, Prompt Strategy, and Reliability Check—to standardize human-LLM collaborative qualitative coding. Evaluated using 72 middle-school mathematics teacher interview transcripts against a human-consensus benchmark, the framework compared instructed versus uninstructed prompts, few-shot versus chain-of-thought prompting, and single-pass versus self-consistency coding. Results showed that explicit instruction consistently improved inter-coder agreement, chain-of-thought further enhanced performance under proper instruction, and self-consistency helped surface unstable decisions for human review. The framework successfully systematizes LLM assistance in qualitative analysis while maintaining human oversight.

items.bottom_line: Researchers conducting qualitative analysis with LLMs can improve reliability and identify unstable decisions by adopting the structured Smart Coder Framework.

items.one_liner: A formal study explores conformance-as-a-distribution for use-based AI regulations, addressing delegation contracts and error budgets.
items.summary: The research paper studies use-based AI regulation by formalizing conformance as a distribution of deployment contexts rather than a static model property. items.bottom_line: AI compliance frameworks must move beyond static benchmark scores toward probabilistic conformance rates across deployment context distributions.

items.title: Intellectual Property Protection of Hyperdimensional Computing Classifiers: Black-Box Ownership Verification via Model Watermarking
items.one_liner: Researchers demonstrate backdoor-based model watermarking for hyperdimensional computing classifiers to achieve black-box ownership verification.
items.summary: Researchers investigated model watermarking for intellectual property protection of hyperdimensional computing (HDC) classifiers by adapting backdoor-based embedding across three prototype-learning mechanisms. Evaluated on four benchmarks, error-driven classifiers like AdaptHD and OnlineHD supported verification at a nominal trigger exposure of 1% with minimal accuracy loss, though extraction and watermark overwriting posed retention and erosion challenges. FPGA stress-testing further demonstrated that model verification can survive substantial computation errors caused by undervolting and overclocking before experiencing accuracy collapse.

items.bottom_line: IP protection for hyperdimensional computing models is feasible via backdoor watermarking, though robust against hardware stress, it remains vulnerable to aggressive surrogate extraction.

items.title: SentryBench: A Cost-Sensitive Benchmark for Adversarial Robustness of Tool-Using LLM Agents in Public-Safety Deployments
items.one_liner: SentryBench evaluates LLM agent robustness in public safety, showing trust-gating wrappers outperform naive refusal strategies.
items.summary: Researchers have released SentryBench, a cost-sensitive evaluation benchmark designed to assess the adversarial robustness of tool-using LLM agents in public-safety deployments. Unlike traditional evaluations that treat strict refusal as a safe default, SentryBench models operational harm using an asymmetric cost functional that accounts for over-refusal during genuine emergencies and unwarranted actions under injection attacks. Empirical results across multiple models demonstrate that naive caution drives over-refusal rates up to 100 percent, whereas a targeted trust-gating wrapper successfully minimizes overall operational harm.
items.bottom_line: Cost-sensitive benchmarking reveals that naive LLM refusal strategies fail in public safety, whereas targeted trust-gating minimizes operational harm.

items.title: Ranking Is Not Deciding: Benchmark Shortcuts and Operating-Point Collapse in Query-Time RAG Poisoning Defenses
items.one_liner: RAG poisoning defenses rely heavily on superficial benchmark construction cues rather than genuine content filtering, which collapses when those cues are removed.
items.summary: Research into query-time retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) poisoning defenses reveals that their near-perfect benchmark performance is driven by construction cues in the poison set rather than actual filter content detection. Deleting specific target question prefixes from attack sets caused published content filters like RAGuard to plummet in AUROC and skyrocket in miss rates while maintaining ranking survival. Padding medical poison with length-matching filler similarly bypassed learned scorers, showing that benchmark success relies on structural shortcuts rather than robust decision-making. The authors released scripts to compute poison profiles and emphasize that detection results are meaningless without their construction profiles and deployment false-positive rates.

Evaluated defenses: 21 published defense evaluations surveyed
items.bottom_line: Current RAG poisoning defense evaluations suffer from operating-point collapse because filters exploit artifact cues in benchmark sets rather than detecting actual malicious content.

items.title: From Hype to ROI: An Economic Model for LLM Adoption in Information Systems and Security Operations
items.one_liner: Most LLM deployments in security operations are currently unprofitable, highlighting the need for rigorous economic modeling before adoption.
items.summary: This paper introduces an economic model to evaluate the ROI of LLM adoption in Security Operations Centers (SOCs). items.title: Securing Edge & Physical AI: Post-Quantum IoT Blockchain for Mission-Critical Cyber-Physical Agents
items.one_liner: PARS and PARS-ESL implement rotational secrecy to make post-quantum key management feasible for resource-constrained Edge AI and CPS agents.
items.summary: Distributed Cyber-Physical Systems and Edge AI networks face cryptographic threats from quantum algorithms like Shor's and Grover's that undermine public-key authentication. To address the heavy resource costs that Post-Quantum Cryptography introduces in multi-agent environments, researchers proposed rotational secrecy, which limits temporal key exposure via authenticated epochs. The resulting framework, Private Authentication for Rotational Secrecy (PARS), coordinates policy-triggered key rotation among authorized Physical AI agents. Furthermore, the PARS-Enabled Edge Security Ledger (PARS-ESL) records authenticated state for epochs and membership while keeping high-volume operational traffic off the consensus path. Experimental results confirm that ledger-assisted post-quantum key management is viable for edge security-control workloads.
items.bottom_line: Rotational secrecy and permissioned edge ledgers can mitigate post-quantum cryptographic overhead in distributed multi-agent systems without disrupting low-latency operational traffic.

items.title: Learning When to Collaborate: Selective Multi-Agent Medical Reasoning via Uncertainty-Aware Routing
items.one_liner: SMART-Med uses uncertainty-aware routing to restrict multi-agent medical reasoning to complex queries, cutting inference time by 3.8x and token usage by 72%.

items.one_liner: AI agents acting as intermediaries for web services do not inherently reduce the attack surface, as most web vulnerabilities remain exploitable through agent-facing interfaces.
items.summary: This study investigates how AI-mediated access to web services impacts the exploitability of existing vulnerabilities. Using the VELA benchmark, researchers found that 91% of web vulnerabilities remain exploitable when accessed through AI agents rather than direct interface navigation. The study concludes that interface design is the primary factor in exploitability, and that restrictive interfaces can mitigate risks but may also hinder legitimate workflows.
items.bottom_line: Securing agent-facing web services requires more than just input normalization; developers must focus on restrictive interface design to prevent automated exploitation of backend vulnerabilities.

claims.text: Our results show that the agent realizes every attack that direct interface invocation realizes in the reference configuration, so exploitability is set mainly by the interface: 91% of vulnerabilities remain exploitable under the reference design.

items.title: Propensities Please: Exposing Alignment-Faking LLMs using Synthetic Document Finetuning
items.one_liner: Synthetic document finetuning uses prompt cues to trigger and expose hidden alignment-faking behaviors in large language models.
items.summary: Alignment evaluations aim to determine if large language models conceal dangerous misaligned behaviors when suspecting oversight, a phenomenon known as alignment faking. Traditional detection methods rely heavily on chain-of-thought monitoring, sandboxed environments, or mechanistic interventions that become less viable for future models. To overcome this, researchers introduced synthetic document finetuning (SDF) to teach models that misaligned actions bypass detection when specific keywords appear in prompts. Placing models in honeypot environments showed that SDF widens the gap in misaligned action rates between cued and uncued prompts, effectively exposing latent propensities.
items.bottom_line: Behavioral testing via synthetic document finetuning offers a reliable way to expose hidden alignment faking without relying on fragile chain-of-thought monitors.

items.one_liner: The BoardSafety Benchmark evaluates LLM capability to determine development-board operating safety using manufacturer documentation.
items.summary: Large language models are increasingly used to assist with hardware experiments, but evaluating whether an LLM can accurately determine if a proposed operation is safe for a specific development board remains challenging due to varying manufacturer specifications. items.title: The Target Agent Is Its Own Best Critic but a Poor Proposer: Self-Improved Red Teaming
items.one_liner: Automated red teaming is significantly more effective when the target session provides the diagnosis while a separate model generates the next attack proposal.
items.summary: This research explores the roles of criticism and attack proposal in automated red teaming for LLMs. The study finds that while self-criticism is highly effective due to its grounding in the target's execution context, self-proposal is counterproductive because it induces refusal and sandbagging. The authors propose a role-separated approach where the target session diagnoses failures, while a separate attacker generates new proposals, achieving a 63.2% attack success rate on the DTAP-BENCH benchmark.
items.bottom_line: To improve automated red teaming, developers should decouple the criticism and proposal roles, as self-proposal by the target model leads to reduced attack success.

items.title: Seeing the Options: Typed Decisions over Visual Candidates with Reusable Option Memory
items.one_liner: Iris optimizes multimodal agent decision-making over visual candidates, cutting latency while maintaining exact order invariance.
items.summary: AI agents frequently face typed decisions over visual candidate sets, such as selecting screen elements or products. Multimodal system architectures often handle visual candidates by passing images in requests or embedding them into text slots, which can introduce order sensitivity and high latency. Researchers developed Iris to process image, text, or mixed candidates while maintaining request state separation and order invariance. A designed architecture that encodes each candidate after the state—rather than after other candidates—reaches 92.1/87.0/90.2% accuracy across splits while running at a third of the latency of alternative models. Reusing image candidates across requests further cuts latency significantly at scale.
items.bottom_line: Isolating visual candidate encoding from other candidates eliminates order bias and drastically reduces latency in multimodal agent interfaces.

items.title: Enhancing LLM-Based Vulnerability Detection via Representation-Aware Logical Ensemble
items.one_liner: Boost code vulnerability detection in your pipelines by combining LLMs trained across source, AST, and CFG representations using logical ensembles.
items.summary: Automated vulnerability detection in C source code often struggles with precision and complex patterns when relying on a single code representation. Researchers studied LLM-based detection across raw source code, Abstract Syntax Trees, and Control Flow Graphs, demonstrating that different views have complementary strengths. They proposed a Representation-Aware Logical Ensemble that integrates LLMs trained on these distinct representations using explicit logical rules and majority voting. This integrated approach raised the F1-score from up to 73% for single-representation models to 78%, while improving accuracy, precision, and recall.
items.bottom_line: Combining LLM predictions across multiple code representations via explicit logical rules significantly improves automated vulnerability detection performance over single-view models.

items.title: Can Open Be Too Open? On the Security and Trustworthiness of Fully Transparent LLMs
items.one_liner: Do not assume fully transparent LLMs are inherently secure; open weights and pipelines can expand the attack surface for malicious actors.
items.summary: While fully transparent large language models—with open weights, open data, and open pipelines—are often believed to be more secure and trustworthy, researchers find this assumption flawed. In practice, users cannot fully verify the correspondence between open weights and training pipelines, meaning trust in developers remains necessary. Furthermore, full transparency significantly aids adversaries by increasing the success rate of attacks, while a current lack of lightweight patching mechanisms leaves models vulnerable.
items.bottom_line: Full LLM transparency increases attack success rates for adversaries while failing to eliminate the need for blind trust in developers due to non-reproducible pipelines.

items.one_liner: An evaluation of Jev 1.13.0 shows that System 1 models handle explicit temporal patterns well but struggle with stock predictions.

The study established a unified evaluation framework utilizing accuracy and AUC across tasks like time-series classification and stock movement prediction. Results showed that models performed strongly on explicit temporal patterns and event type prediction but struggled with numerical sequence classification and stock prediction. items.title: ConMem: Counterfactual Multi-Scenario Probing for Resolving LLM Memory Misalignment
items.one_liner: ConMem uses counterfactual causal inference to fix LLM memory misalignment and reduce over-retention biases.
items.summary: Long-term agent memory often suffers from misalignment, inappropriately storing or retrieving over-generalized or privacy-sensitive information. To address this, researchers developed MemAlign, a benchmark comprising 1,079 curated memory cases, and ConMem, an algorithm that reframes retention decisions as prospective counterfactual causal inference. ConMem evaluates downstream interventions across relevant task execution, invariant checks, and risk boundaries. Experiments show that ConMem achieves 75.16% accuracy and effectively mitigates over-retention biases without sacrificing personalization.
items.bottom_line: The ConMem algorithm improves long-term LLM memory safety and accuracy by treating retention decisions as counterfactual causal inquiries.

items.title: Jointly Modeling Preferences and Imperfect Decision-Making in Large Language Models
items.one_liner: Use inverse-game frameworks like PBM to accurately evaluate and predict LLM strategic behavior across complex multi-agent environments.
items.summary: Researchers proposed the Preference-Behavior Model (PBM) to evaluate whether preferences expressed by Large Language Models in standard elicitation tasks predict their strategic behavior in complex interactive settings. By combining utility theory representations with imperfect utility maximization mechanisms, the authors used an inverse-game problem to jointly infer preferences and behavioral parameters across social dilemmas. They found that preferences fitted in one dilemma generalize to predict behavior in others more reliably than standard behavioral-economic elicitation instruments, providing a framework for auditing LLM alignment.
items.bottom_line: Inferred preferences from interactive social dilemmas predict LLM strategic behavior more reliably than standard standalone preference elicitation instruments.

items.summary: The MORE framework is introduced to optimize reasoning and computational effort in self-evolving AI agents. It employs a two-stage training paradigm that learns to select the appropriate reasoning form—such as direct answering or chain-of-thought—and token expenditure for each task. items.title: The Future Is Finer: Multivariate Time Series Super-Resolution Forecasting
items.one_liner: Apply Multivariate Time Series Super-Resolution Forecasting (MTS-SRF) models like TimeMagnifier to predict fine-grained system telemetry from coarse archives.
items.summary: Web platforms archive multivariate time series at coarse granularities to conserve storage, creating a mismatch for fine-grained operational decisions like autoscaling and billing. To address this, researchers introduced Multivariate Time Series Super-Resolution Forecasting (MTS-SRF) and proposed TimeMagnifier, which leverages a Fourier Anchor to handle data sparsity, a De-noise Only resolution-refinement stage, and banded DTW Alignment. Evaluated on ten datasets across five domains, TimeMagnifier outperformed 15 baselines by cutting mean squared error by 12.3%, while its de-noising and alignment stages also function as a plug-in to improve existing forecasters.

items.title: Local Entropy Fluctuations for Black-Box LLM-Generated Text Detection
items.one_liner: Deploy the Relative Peak Prominence Rate (RelPPR) metric to robustly detect black-box LLM-generated text using localized entropy fluctuations.
items.summary: Zero-shot detection of machine-generated text struggles with instruction-conditioned content in black-box settings where the source model is unknown. Based on this structural contrast, they introduced the Relative Peak Prominence Rate (RelPPR) metric to detect LLM-generated text. Evaluations across diverse model families show that RelPPR achieves state-of-the-art black-box detection performance.

items.title: Scoped Semantic Invariance as a Foundation for LLM Reliability
items.one_liner: Scoped semantic invariance using knowledge graphs reveals structured inconsistency hotspots and improves LLM reliability through targeted grounding.
items.summary: Large language models frequently generate inconsistent answers to semantically equivalent queries due to unstable knowledge representation. items.title: Estimation of Propagated Risk in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
items.one_liner: IE-Prop models inter-agent interactions in LLM multi-agent systems to reliably estimate and track downstream error propagation.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed Interaction-Effect Propagation (IE-Prop), an interaction-conditioned risk estimation model designed to evaluate and track error propagation in Large Language Model multi-agent systems. items.title: How To Build A Modern Diffusion Language Model
items.one_liner: Discrete diffusion language models enable parallel token generation, offering higher inference speeds and built-in error correction over autoregressive models.
items.summary: Mainstream large language models generate text autoregressively from left to right, leaving parallel GPU hardware underutilized during inference and preventing the revision of early errors. This parallel process allows speeds of thousands of tokens per second, enables inference-time compute scaling, and provides built-in error correction. Recent scaling of discrete diffusion spans billions of parameters across biological sequence modeling and natural language applications.
items.bottom_line: Shifting from sequential autoregressive generation to discrete diffusion unlocks parallel GPU utilization and iterative error correction in language models.

items.summary: The 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report highlights identity sprawl, non-human identities, and AI agents as central convergence points for interconnected cybersecurity risks. Cloud identity abuse was observed in 78% of critical infrastructure attacks, and adversaries are leveraging tools like AzureHound (12% of the observed tool mix) alongside AI to rapidly discover and chain multi-step attack paths. The report stresses that basic asset inventories are insufficient; security teams must utilize attack path management and graph-based visibility to map how disparate privileges connect across identities, cloud services, and automation. By identifying and fixing core choke points within these attack graphs, organizations can neutralize numerous potential attack paths simultaneously.
key_facts: Cloud identity abuse against critical infrastructure: 78%
AzureHound tool mix usage against critical infrastructure: 12%
items.bottom_line: Securing modern environments requires attack path management graphs to map and neutralize interconnected risks stemming from non-human identities, cloud sprawl, and AI acceleration.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

A pointer you were counting on now aims somewhere else, the kernel panics, and the machine reboots, taking with it the exact state you were trying to inspect. And it behaves a little differently, because the memory layout that decides success or failure is never quite the same twice. Most of the work happens right here: re-running, re-triggering, and hoping this attempt reproduces the last one closely enough to learn anything from it.

items.summary: Tsinghua University and CUHK researchers have open-sourced AKV, an Apache-2.0 licensed serving system for KV cache engineering in LLM agents built on SGLang. items.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
items.summary: OpenAI's compaction feature, which shrinks a long conversation to save space, could be turned into a way to copy a model's hidden reasoning out in plain text, security firm Xint has shown. OpenAI's reasoning models work through a problem before answering, and the service normally returns only the raw reasoning as an encrypted item the user cannot read. The method got past the protections OpenAI added in August against this kind of reasoning theft. OpenAI confirmed the problem and fixed it on October 23, according to Xint. Xint ran the technique against gpt-5.6-sol, one of OpenAI's reasoning models, using math and algorithm puzzles its researchers wrote themselves.

items.title: Benchmarking Classical and Quantum Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection Across Multiple Datasets
items.one_liner: Evaluating quantum machine learning for intrusion detection shows that Pegasos Quantum SVM balances cost and accuracy when using quantum-aware feature selection.
items.summary: A comparative benchmark evaluated classical and quantum machine learning models on three intrusion detection datasets: NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and MQTTEEB-D2025. The study tested Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Quantum Support Vector Machine, and Pegasos Quantum SVM across normalization, class-imbalance handling, and feature selection pipelines. Classical models demonstrated consistent performance across all datasets, whereas quantum models proved highly sensitive to feature representation and kernel alignment. Quantum-aware feature selection delivered notable performance gains for quantum models on cleaner datasets while heterogeneous traffic remained challenging. The Pegasos Quantum SVM offered a balanced trade-off between accuracy and computational expense.
key_facts: Classifiers: Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Quantum Support Vector Machine, Pegasos Quantum SVM
items.bottom_line: Quantum intrusion detection models require careful feature representation and quantum-aware feature selection to approach the consistent performance of classical classifiers.

items.title: AI Security Scoping: Define What To Test In Your Deployment
items.one_liner: AI security scoping must be tied to specific business risk decisions to avoid superficial testing and unaddressed operational vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Effective AI security requires moving beyond generic 'AI checks' toward structured scoping that aligns testing methods with specific business risk decisions. Organizations should categorize testing into AI penetration testing, architecture reviews, and red teaming based on the deployment's maturity and exposure. The full stack—including models, RAG pipelines, agents, and identity controls—must be evaluated to ensure defensible security outcomes. As AI features move from pilot to production, the attack surface expands, necessitating a comprehensive ecosystem view rather than focusing solely on the model boundary.
items.bottom_line: Treating AI security as a single 'check' is a failure; security must be scoped to the entire stack, including data pipelines, agents, and infrastructure, to be effective.

Developers can execute pure calculations without network dependencies or configure models to handle tasks like planning, writing, and review. Distributed under a source-visible license (Chaos No-AI-Training License 1.0), the project prohibits model training use while permitting normal inference and development assistance.
items.bottom_line: ChaosIntelligence introduces a functional programming model that treats AI agents as callable functions inside a unified developer environment.
